{"type":"tool_result","timestamp":"2026-11-12T00:09:39.519Z","tool_id":"mcp_lore_lore_assemble_context__call_18416120107524402519","status":"success","output":"<context query=\"Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema\" template=\"default\" budget=\"8000\">\n<section name=\"Conventions\" source=\"repo\" priority=\"1\">\n<document source=\"specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md\" type=\"spec\" relevance=\"1.00\" tokens=\"215\">\nStatus: implemented\n## Validation contract\n- `execute` validates `input` against the resolved tool definition's `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked ([validated by: returns a ToolResponse naming the missing required field and does not invoke the executor @beecb068](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L10)).\n## Schema compilation\n- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time; an uncompilable schema causes `register` to throw synchronously with a message that names the tool, so a broken schema fails at startup rather than mid-conversation ([validated by: throws at register time when the inputSchema is uncompilable and the message names the tool @8d00dfb3](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L73)).\n</document>\n<document source=\"CHANGELOG.md\" type=\"doc\" relevance=\"0.95\" tokens=\"64\">\n## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-29\n- `ToolRegistry.execute` now validates tool input against each tool's `inputSchema`, so a tool that produced its own message for malformed input receives only valid input; FIX: use a dynamic `const { fn } = await import(\\\"./spec-pr.js\\\")` inside the test instead of a static import, and append the describe block AFTER the last test — zero line shift, zero anchor breakage. (2) re-lint/max-comment-lines bans comments in test files entirely — put meaning in the it() name, not a comment. A RED parallel-change test of a not-yet-exported symbol DOES produce one intended `tsc` error (Property X does not exist); that's the deliverable, not a mistake.\",\"score\":0.860241269994918,\"agent_id\":\"3277b0be-0a76-41fb-bda1-a4005e903a96\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"},{\"key\":\"consolidated/re-cinq-bowman-ui#17/1787722212522\",\"value\":\"Configuration and contract enforcement are decoupled; eslint rules, documentation, and actual validation can drift (e.g., 't' banned in CONTRACT.md but not enforced in eslint config), requiring periodic audits to catch gaps.\",\"score\":0.7989710789766405,\"agent_id\":\"consolidation\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"},{\"key\":\"consolidated/re-cinq-lore#307,#308,#310,#311,#312,#313/1777959021438\",\"value\":\"Symlinked workspace dependencies (node_modules/@re-cinq/lore-shared → ../../shared) and declarative workflow YAML (4 node types, 4 edge conditions) are rigid path/schema contracts—document exact paths and enforce schema validation early, since import failures are silent and workflow misconfiguration cascades across all automation.\",\"score\":0.7724855560905151,\"agent_id\":\"consolidation\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"},{\"key\":\"review/fix-validate-builds-workspaces-2026-08-30\",\"value\":\"PR #1676 (fix/validate-builds-workspaces, 2026-08-30): detectNode in repo-validation.ts now hoists the `build` step before `lint` when (a) the fresh-clone guard fires and (b) `package.json` declares `workspaces` as an array. Root cause: commit b219a4f1 saw `npm ci` succeed but eslint fail with `cannot import @re-cinq/lore-shared/spec-status.js` because the ESLint plugin imports a workspace package's compiled dist, which an install does not produce. The fix moves (never duplicates) the existing build step and bumps its timeout to 300_000ms (cold-clone budget). Gate: `Array.isArray(pkg.workspaces)` — the npm object-form `{ packages: [...] }` is NOT covered (rare in practice). fullChecks inherits via `[...quick, ...full]`. Six tests added covering all guard conditions. Spec FR updated with new test links.\",\"score\":0.7480671820847773,\"agent_id\":\"952b6c2e-243f-41e6-af64-10cb45440f82\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"},{\"key\":\"consolidated/unknown/1789018253927\",\"value\":\"Queuing strategies and rule applicability vary by repository topology and team convention — monorepo tools (no-cross-layer-import) cannot govern single-package layouts, ESLint preset auto-updates risk silent breakage with --max-warnings 0, and teams must choose between hand-wired rules (re-cinq convention) or ratchet scripts for on-demand drain. Future agents adopting linting rules should map repository structure, audit canary tests, and explicitly document which rules are parked and why before merging rule changes.\",\"score\":0.7254396389362002,\"agent_id\":\"consolidation\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"},{\"key\":\"consolidated/re-cinq-bowman-ui#1/1787722219206\",\"value\":\"ESLint rules are underenforced relative to specification requirements (exhaustive-deps and no-explicit-any configured as warn instead of error). This allows non-compliant code to merge. Future agents should audit all ESLint configurations against the specification and upgrade violations from warn to error for any rules tied to public API quality or correctness guarantees.\",\"score\":0.7118954553295591,\"agent_id\":\"consolidation\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"},{\"key\":\"consolidated/re-cinq-lore/1793511006500\",\"value\":\"Build and test quality regressions are caught through layered verification workflows (CI tests, TypeScript compilation, code review, recheckable specs), and union type narrowing with enforceTrue is the standard fix for type system blockages in test files.\",\"score\":0.6924324324324324,\"agent_id\":\"consolidation\",\"source\":\"memory\",\"backend\":\"utopia\"}],\"notes\":[]}"}

validation\n\ndiff --git a/.lore/dod.md b/.lore/dod.md\nnew file mode 100644\nindex 0000000..c48641a\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/.lore/dod.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@\n+# Definition of Done\n+\n+> `ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor\n+> without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).\n+> Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both\n+> providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model.\n+\n+**Strategy: `direct`** — `ToolRegistry.register`, `ToolRegistry.execute` and `createChatOrchestrator` already expose the exact entry points this ticket changes, so the acceptance tests call them directly today and fail because schema compilation and input validation are absent.\n+\n+## Done when these pass\n+\n+- [ ] **rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor** — `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against `inputSchema`, returns a `ToolResponse` naming the missing required property, and does not invoke the executor.\n+  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`\n+\n+- [ ] **rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs** — `ToolRegistry.execute` rejects a property with the wrong JSON Schema type without calling the executor, names the failing field path and expected type in `result`, and omits the offending property value from both `result` and emitted log lines.\n+  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`\n+\n+- [ ] **throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled** — `ToolRegistry.register` compiles a static `ToolDefinition`'s `inputSchema` once at registration time and throws synchronously naming the tool when the schema is invalid.\n+  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`\n+\n+- [ ] **returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round** — `createChatOrchestrator` feeds a schema-rejected tool call's `ToolResponse.result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` without invoking the executor on the invalid call, allowing the model to retry with valid arguments and complete the turn.\n+  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`\n+\n+## Facets\n+\n+- [ ] Add `ajv` to `dependencies` in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (`strict: false`, `validateFormats: false`, no coercion, no defaults, no injected `additionalProperties: false`) and bump the package version `MINOR`.\n+- [ ] Compile static `ToolDefinition.inputSchema` at `ToolRegistry.register` time (throwing an error naming the tool on invalid schemas) and cache compiled validators for function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` schemas by schema object reference (`WeakMap`).\n+- [ ] Validate `input` in `ToolRegistry.execute` before invoking the executor, returning a `ToolResponse` (`{result}`) that names failing field paths and expected types/required fields without echoing or logging offending values, and add the one-line doc comment pointing at `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`.\n+- [ ] Add unit tests in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` and `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`, link the remaining statements in `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, and update `example/weather-tool.ts`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md`, `.specify/spec.md`, `adrs/ADR-002-response-validation.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.\n+\n+## Out of scope\n+\n+- Output validation and domain sanity checks (covered by ADR-002), MCP tool-server discovery and proxying (#42), per-tool authorization or `beforeToolCall` hooks (#40), retry/timeout/rate-limiting around tool execution, and concrete tool implementations.\ndiff --git a/specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md b/specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md\nnew file mode 100644\nindex 0000000..6986bfe\n--- /dev/null\n+++ b/specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md\n@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@\n+# Tool Input Validation\n+\n+| Field  | Value                |\n+| ------ | -------------------- |\n+| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n+| Status | In Progress          |\n+\n+Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n+\n+## Validation at execute time\n+\n+- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).\n+- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n+- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults.\n+- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.\n+\n+## Schema compilation and caching\n+\n+- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94)).\n+- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema`.\n+- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules.\n+\n+## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n+\n+- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).\ndiff --git b/src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts\n@@ -0,0 +1,183 @@\n+import {ToolRegistry} from './registry.js';\n+import {createChatOrchestrator} from '../chatOrchestrator.js';\n+import {PromptBuilder} from '../../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\n+import {setLogger} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n+import type {Logger} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n+import type {AIProvider, MessageChunk, SendMessageParams, ToolResultMessage} from '../../types/ai.js';\n+import type {ChatSession} from '../../types/session.js';\n+\n+const SENT_AT = '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';\n+\n+describe('ToolRegistry inputSchema validation acceptance', () => {\n+  afterEach(() => {\n+    setLogger(undefined);\n+  });\n+\n+  it('rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor', async () => {\n+    const registry = new ToolRegistry();\n+    let executorCalls = 0;\n+    registry.register(\n+      {\n+        name: 'get_weather',\n+        description: 'Get weather for a location',\n+        inputSchema: {\n+          type: 'object',\n+          properties: {location: {type: 'string'}},\n+          required: ['location'],\n+        },\n+      },\n+      async () => {\n+        executorCalls += 1;\n+        return 'sunny';\n+      }\n+    );\n+\n+    const response = await registry.execute('get_weather', {});\n+\n+    expect({\n+      executorCalls,\n+      mentionsRequiredField: response.result.includes('location') && /required/i.test(response.result),\n+    }).toEqual({\n+      executorCalls: 0,\n+      mentionsRequiredField: true,\n+    });\n+  });\n+\n+  it('rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs', async () => {\n+    const recordedLogs: string[] = [];\n+    const recordLine = (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) => {\n+      recordedLogs.push(JSON.stringify({category, message, fields}));\n+    };\n+    const logger: Logger = {\n+      debug: recordLine,\n+      info: recordLine,\n+      warn: recordLine,\n+      error: recordLine,\n+    };\n+    setLogger(logger);\n+\n+    const registry = new ToolRegistry();\n+    let executorCalls = 0;\n+    registry.register(\n+      {\n+        name: 'ssn_lookup',\n+        description: 'Look up record by identifier',\n+        inputSchema: {\n+          type: 'object',\n+          properties: {ssn: {type: 'string'}},\n+          required: ['ssn'],\n+        },\n+      },\n+      async () => {\n+        executorCalls += 1;\n+        return 'found';\n+      }\n+    );\n+\n+    const response = await registry.execute('ssn_lookup', {ssn: 123456789});\n+\n+    expect({\n+      executorCalls,\n+      mentionsField: response.result.includes('ssn'),\n+      mentionsExpectedType: response.result.includes('string'),\n+      leaksValueInResult: response.result.includes('123456789'),\n+      leaksValueInLogs: recordedLogs.some(line => line.includes('123456789')),\n+    }).toEqual({\n+      executorCalls: 0,\n+      mentionsField: true,\n+      mentionsExpectedType: true,\n+      leaksValueInResult: false,\n+      leaksValueInLogs: false,\n+    });\n+  });\n+\n+  it('throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled', () => {\n+    const registry = new ToolRegistry();\n+\n+    expect(() =>\n+      registry.register(\n+        {\n+          name: 'broken_weather',\n+          description: 'Has an invalid JSON Schema type',\n+          inputSchema: {\n+            type: 'object',\n+            properties: {location: {type: 'not-a-json-schema-type'}},\n+          },\n+        },\n+        async () => 'unreachable'\n+      )\n+    ).toThrow(/broken_weather/);\n+  });\n+\n+  it('returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round', async () => {\n+    const registry = new ToolRegistry();\n+    const executorInputs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> = [];\n+    registry.register(\n+      () => ({\n+        name: 'get_weather',\n+        description: 'Get weather for a location',\n+        inputSchema: {\n+          type: 'object',\n+          properties: {location: {type: 'string'}},\n+          required: ['location'],\n+        },\n+      }),\n+      async input => {\n+        executorInputs.push(input);\n+        return `22C in ${String(input.location)}`;\n+      }\n+    );\n+\n+    let firstRoundToolResult = '';\n+    let round = 0;\n+    const provider: AIProvider = {\n+      async *sendMessage(params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n+        round += 1;\n+        if (round === 1) {\n+          yield {type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'call-1', name: 'get_weather', input: {}}};\n+          yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'tool_use'};\n+          return;\n+        }\n+        if (round === 2) {\n+          const lastMessage = params.messages[params.messages.length - 1] as ToolResultMessage;\n+          firstRoundToolResult = lastMessage.content[0]?.content ?? '';\n+          yield {\n+            type: 'tool_use',\n+            toolCall: {id: 'call-2', name: 'get_weather', input: {location: 'Paris'}},\n+          };\n+          yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'tool_use'};\n+          return;\n+        }\n+        yield {type: 'text', text: '22C in Paris'};\n+        yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n+      },\n+      async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n+        return {} as T;\n+      },\n+    };\n+\n+    const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(\n+      provider,\n+      new PromptBuilder({identity: 'You are a test assistant.'}),\n+      registry\n+    );\n+    const session: ChatSession = {\n+      sessionId: 's-retry',\n+      userId: 'u1',\n+      entries: [{role: 'user', content: 'Weather in Paris?', timestamp: SENT_AT}],\n+    };\n+\n+    const reply = await orchestrator.processMessage(session);\n+\n+    expect({\n+      reply,\n+      executorInputs,\n+      firstAttemptRejectedForLocation:\n+        firstRoundToolResult.includes('location') && /required/i.test(firstRoundToolResult),\n+    }).toEqual({\n+      reply: '22C in Paris',\n+      executorInputs: [{location: 'Paris'}],\n+      firstAttemptRejectedForLocation: true,\n+    });\n+  });\n+});"}
